newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 17.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - A report from the Bertelsmann Research Foundation released in Prague on Thursday said that none of the western or eastern European countries who want membership in the EU have fulfilled all conditions. The foundation commended favourable macroeconomic results in the Czech Republic, but also showed not enough restructuring of businesses, low work productivity and little expansion of capital markets and the banking sector.

- The main complication in the approval of the Czech-German Declaration is the German responsibility for the break-up of the Czechoslovak Republic in 1938 and the subsequent Nazi invasion and the regret expressed to the Czech Republic for these actions from the German side.
- Interest rates on bank credit, which are growing two or three times as fast as the economy, have not recorded any significant declines this year.
- Foreign exchange profits from the travel industry are growing every year, and the Czech Republic is beginning to aspire to be placed among the top 20 countries with the largest exchange flows.

PRAVO - EuroTel is having problems with signals from mobile telephone network GSM and with the quality of the network, which is making the company unable to fulfill the licence conditions which it agreed to during its trial period with GSM. EuroTel's GSM signal currently covers 65 percent of the Czech Republic with 76 percent of the population, but the licence requires the signal to cover 80 percent of the population by the end of June.

- Members of the budget committee of parliament decided yesterday that changes in the legislative system are necessary for further expansion of the activities of Export Guarantee and Insurance Company (EGAP) and Ceska Exportni Banka.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - If the government determines to go through with the plan to deregulate prices of energy and also makes amends to certain tax charges this year, it will of course mean that the government by law will have to modify incomes twice. The first change is expected in July, and the second in December.
- Health Minister Miroslav Macek publicised new and more concrete plans regarding health reforms yesterday, two months since Macek's first proposal did not succeed due to a few points.
